title: Indian Banking History
subtitle: IBPS SO / RRB SO Exam Practice
source: Bank SO IT exam-oriented question bank; reference lessons used only for topic scope.
instructions: Choose the best answer. Questions are independently authored for competitive-exam practice.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India commenced operations on:
questions.explanation: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse the commencement date with the date of nationalisation in 1949.
questions.hint: Recall the year in which the central bank began operations.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India was established under which legislation?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India was constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
questions.importantPoint: RBI Act, 1934 is the founding statute.
questions.examTrap: The Banking Regulation Act is important for banking regulation but did not establish RBI.
questions.hint: Identify the statute named after the central bank.

questions.question: RBI was originally set up as a:

options.text: Department of the Ministry of Finance

questions.explanation: The RBI was initially privately held and was nationalised in 1949.
questions.examTrap: Do not project its present ownership status backward to 1935.
questions.hint: Think about what changed in 1949.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in:
questions.explanation: The RBI was nationalised in 1949, making it wholly owned by the Government of India.
questions.examTrap: 1947 is Independence, not RBI nationalisation.
questions.hint: Separate the political milestone of Independence from the banking milestone.

questions.question: The first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India was:
questions.explanation: Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of the RBI.
questions.importantPoint: First RBI Governor: Sir Osborne Smith.
questions.examTrap: C. D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor, not the first Governor overall.
questions.hint: Distinguish first Governor from first Indian Governor.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian Governor of the RBI?
questions.explanation: C. D. Deshmukh became the first Indian Governor of the RBI.
questions.importantPoint: First Indian RBI Governor: C. D. Deshmukh.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse him with the first Governor, Osborne Smith.
questions.hint: Focus on the word “Indian”.

questions.question: The headquarters of the RBI is located in:
questions.explanation: The RBI’s central office is in Mumbai.
questions.examTrap: Kolkata was historically important to banking but is not RBI headquarters.
questions.hint: Think of the RBI Central Office location.

questions.question: Which institution was established in 1949 to regulate banking companies in India?

options.text: Reserve Bank of India under the Banking Regulation framework

questions.explanation: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provided the statutory framework for regulation of banking companies by RBI.
questions.examTrap: NABARD and SIDBI were established decades later.
questions.hint: Focus on the year 1949 and banking regulation.

questions.question: The Imperial Bank of India was transformed into the State Bank of India in:
questions.explanation: The State Bank of India Act, 1955 led to the establishment of SBI from the Imperial Bank of India.
questions.examTrap: 1969 relates to the first major bank nationalisation wave.
questions.hint: Link the Imperial Bank with SBI.

questions.question: The State Bank of India was established under:
questions.explanation: SBI was constituted under the State Bank of India Act, 1955.
questions.examTrap: The 1969 nationalisation wave involved other major banks, not the original creation of SBI.
questions.hint: Recall the legislation that created SBI.

questions.question: The first major nationalisation of 14 banks in India took place in:
questions.explanation: Fourteen major commercial banks were nationalised in 1969.
questions.examTrap: 1980 was the second major nationalisation wave involving six banks.
questions.hint: Remember the 14-bank milestone.

questions.question: How many major commercial banks were nationalised in the first 1969 nationalisation wave?
questions.explanation: The 1969 nationalisation covered 14 major commercial banks.
questions.examTrap: Six banks were nationalised in the second wave in 1980.
questions.hint: Compare 1969 and 1980.

questions.question: The second major nationalisation of banks took place in:
questions.explanation: Six additional commercial banks were nationalised in 1980.
questions.examTrap: 1991 marks economic reforms, not the second nationalisation wave.
questions.hint: Think of the second nationalisation milestone.

questions.question: How many banks were nationalised in the 1980 wave?
questions.explanation: Six more banks were nationalised in 1980.
questions.examTrap: Do not interchange the 1969 and 1980 counts.
questions.hint: Compare the two nationalisation waves.

questions.question: The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced in:
questions.explanation: The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced in 1969 to improve banking development and credit planning at the district level.
questions.examTrap: It is not a post-1991 reform.
questions.hint: Associate the scheme with the first nationalisation period.

questions.question: The Regional Rural Banks were established under which Act?
questions.explanation: RRBs were established under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
questions.examTrap: NABARD was established later in 1982.
questions.hint: Look for the legislation specifically named for RRBs.

questions.question: Regional Rural Banks were established with the objective of primarily serving:
questions.explanation: RRBs were created to improve institutional credit access in rural areas, particularly for agriculture and weaker sections.
questions.examTrap: RRBs are not designed primarily for capital-market intermediation.
questions.hint: Think about the “Rural” in RRB.

questions.question: NABARD was established in:
questions.explanation: NABARD was established on 12 July 1982.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse its year with the RRB Act of 1976.
questions.hint: Recall the apex rural-development institution’s founding year.

questions.question: NABARD was established under:
questions.explanation: NABARD was created under the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981 and commenced operations in 1982.
questions.examTrap: The Act year and commencement year are different.
questions.hint: Distinguish legislation from commencement.

questions.question: SIDBI was established in:
questions.explanation: SIDBI was established on 2 April 1990 as the principal financial institution for promotion, financing and development of the MSME sector.
questions.examTrap: 1991 is associated with economic reforms, not SIDBI’s establishment.
questions.hint: Think of the institution focused on small industries.

questions.question: SIDBI primarily focuses on:
questions.explanation: SIDBI is the principal financial institution for promotion, financing and development of the MSME sector.
questions.examTrap: Agricultural and rural-development finance is associated more directly with NABARD.
questions.hint: Match the institution with its sector.

questions.question: The economic reforms that significantly changed India’s financial sector began in:
questions.explanation: The 1991 reforms introduced major liberalisation measures, including changes affecting the financial sector.
questions.examTrap: 1991 did not mark the beginning of bank nationalisation.
questions.hint: Associate 1991 with liberalisation.

questions.question: The Narasimham Committee of 1991 was primarily associated with reforms in:
questions.explanation: The Committee on the Financial System headed by M. Narasimham examined banking and financial-sector reforms.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse it with committees dealing with unrelated sectors.
questions.hint: Think “financial system”.

questions.question: The Narasimham Committee II was constituted in:
questions.explanation: The second Narasimham Committee was constituted in 1998 to review banking-sector reforms.
questions.examTrap: 1991 refers to the first committee.
questions.hint: Distinguish Committee I and II.

questions.question: Which committee is closely associated with the introduction of prudential norms in Indian banking reforms?
questions.explanation: The Narasimham Committee recommendations were central to banking-sector reforms, including prudential norms and income recognition concepts.
questions.examTrap: The other committees had different mandates.
questions.hint: Focus on banking-sector reform.

questions.question: The Banking Ombudsman Scheme was introduced by RBI in:
questions.explanation: The RBI introduced the Banking Ombudsman Scheme in 1995 to provide a mechanism for resolving customer complaints against banks.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse the original scheme with later revisions.
questions.hint: Recall the first introduction year.

questions.question: The first bank to be established in India is commonly identified as:
questions.explanation: Bank of Hindustan, established in 1770, is commonly cited as the first bank established in India.
questions.examTrap: SBI and PNB were established much later.
questions.hint: Think of the earliest commonly cited bank.

questions.question: Which was the first presidency bank?
questions.explanation: Bank of Bengal was established in 1806 and was the first of the three Presidency Banks.
questions.examTrap: Bank of Bombay and Bank of Madras followed later.
questions.hint: Recall the chronological order of Presidency Banks.

questions.question: Bank of Bombay was established in:
questions.explanation: Bank of Bombay was established in 1840.
questions.examTrap: 1843 corresponds to Bank of Madras.
questions.hint: Compare the establishment years of the Presidency Banks.

questions.question: Bank of Madras was established in:
questions.explanation: Bank of Madras was established in 1843.
questions.examTrap: Do not swap Bombay and Madras.
questions.hint: Recall the sequence: Bengal, Bombay, Madras.

questions.question: The three Presidency Banks were amalgamated in 1921 to form:
questions.explanation: The Bank of Bengal, Bank of Bombay and Bank of Madras were amalgamated in 1921 to form the Imperial Bank of India.
questions.examTrap: SBI came later in 1955.
questions.hint: Identify the institution that preceded SBI.

questions.question: The Imperial Bank of India was formed in:
questions.explanation: The Imperial Bank of India was formed in 1921 by amalgamating the three Presidency Banks.
questions.examTrap: 1955 is the year it became SBI.
questions.hint: Separate formation of Imperial Bank from its later conversion.

questions.question: The first Indian bank with limited liability established by Indians is commonly identified as:
questions.explanation: Allahabad Bank, established in 1865, is commonly described in banking histories as the oldest joint-stock bank in India still in existence for much of its history.
questions.examTrap: Avoid confusing it with PNB (1894).
questions.hint: Compare the historical establishment years.

questions.question: Punjab National Bank was established in:
questions.explanation: Punjab National Bank was established in 1894.
questions.examTrap: Allahabad Bank predates it.
questions.hint: Recall PNB’s 19th-century founding.

questions.question: Bank of India was established in:
questions.explanation: Bank of India was established in 1906.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse 1906 with the Swadeshi-era banking expansion generally.
questions.hint: Recall the year of establishment.

questions.question: Central Bank of India was established in:
questions.explanation: Central Bank of India was established in 1911.
questions.examTrap: 1921 is the Imperial Bank milestone.
questions.hint: Compare the dates of major Indian banks.

questions.question: The Banking Companies Act, 1949 was later renamed as the:
questions.explanation: The Banking Companies Act, 1949 was renamed the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
questions.examTrap: It is not the same legislation as the RBI Act, 1934.
questions.hint: Look for the standard current name of the Act.

questions.question: The State Bank of India group was expanded through the nationalisation of:
questions.explanation: Seven associate banks were brought into the SBI group in 1960 under the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959.
questions.examTrap: The 1969 nationalisation involved 14 major commercial banks.
questions.hint: Separate SBI expansion from nationalisation.

questions.question: The first phase of bank nationalisation in 1969 was based on the banking nationalisation ordinance issued by:
questions.explanation: The Government of India nationalised 14 major banks in 1969.
questions.importantPoint: 1969 nationalisation was a government policy action.
questions.examTrap: RBI is the central bank and regulator, but the nationalisation decision was by the government.
questions.hint: Focus on who enacted nationalisation.

questions.question: Which development is most directly associated with the 1990s banking reforms?

options.text: Creation of the first Presidency Bank

questions.explanation: The 1990s reforms strengthened prudential norms and introduced greater competition through banking-sector liberalisation.
questions.examTrap: Nationalisation belongs to 1969/1980.
questions.hint: Think of post-1991 liberalisation.

questions.question: The concept of “priority sector lending” is most closely connected with the objective of:

options.text: Directing credit toward identified priority sectors

questions.explanation: Priority sector lending channels a prescribed share of bank credit toward sectors considered important for inclusive economic development.
questions.importantPoint: Priority sector lending supports identified priority sectors.
questions.examTrap: It is not limited to large corporate lending.
questions.hint: Focus on the policy objective of directed credit.

questions.question: Which institution succeeded the Industrial Finance Corporation of India as part of the development-finance landscape?

options.text: No direct successor; IFCI remained a distinct institution

questions.explanation: IFCI remained a distinct development financial institution; it was not succeeded by NABARD or SEBI.
questions.examTrap: NABARD and SEBI have different mandates and histories.
questions.hint: Check whether the premise implies a formal successor.

questions.question: SEBI received statutory status in:
questions.explanation: SEBI was established in 1988 and received statutory powers under the SEBI Act, 1992.
questions.examTrap: Do not state simply that SEBI was “created” in 1992 without the distinction.
questions.hint: Separate establishment from statutory status.

questions.question: Which institution regulates India’s securities market?
questions.explanation: SEBI is the statutory regulator of India’s securities market.
questions.examTrap: RBI regulates monetary and banking matters, not the securities market generally.
questions.hint: Match regulator to market.

questions.question: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act was enacted in:
questions.explanation: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 provides the legal framework for regulation and supervision of payment systems in India.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse it with the 2013 Companies Act.
questions.hint: Think of the legal framework for payment systems.

questions.question: The Monetary Policy Committee was formally constituted in its present statutory framework in:
questions.explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee framework was established through amendments to the RBI Act in 2016.
questions.examTrap: The policy rate framework existed before the statutory MPC.
questions.hint: Focus on the formal MPC framework.

questions.question: Which institution is responsible for monetary policy in India?
questions.explanation: The RBI is entrusted with the formulation and implementation of monetary policy in India.
questions.examTrap: SEBI regulates securities markets.
questions.hint: Match the institution to monetary policy.

questions.question: The Nationalisation of banks in 1969 was primarily aimed at:

options.text: Expanding banking access and aligning credit with development priorities
Replacing RBI with a new central bank

questions.explanation: The 1969 nationalisation was associated with wider banking access, branch expansion and directing credit toward development priorities.
questions.importantPoint: Nationalisation expanded the developmental role of banking.
questions.examTrap: It was not a privatisation programme.
questions.hint: Consider the stated development objectives of the period.

questions.question: Which sequence is chronologically correct?
questions.explanation: RBI operations began in 1935, while SBI was established in 1955 from the Imperial Bank formed in 1921; therefore the proposed sequence in A is not chronologically complete.
questions.importantPoint: Chronology questions require checking every event, not just one pair.
questions.examTrap: Option A actually omits the Imperial Bank-to-SBI relationship and is therefore not a valid chronological sequence.
questions.hint: Check all three dates carefully.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders these milestones from earliest to latest?

options.text: Bank of Bengal → Imperial Bank of India → RBI operations → SBI
RBI operations → Bank of Bengal → Imperial Bank of India → SBI
Bank of Bengal → RBI operations → SBI → Imperial Bank of India
Imperial Bank of India → Bank of Bengal → RBI operations → SBI

questions.explanation: Bank of Bengal was established in 1806, the Imperial Bank was formed in 1921, RBI began operations in 1935, and SBI was established in 1955.
questions.examTrap: Do not place RBI before the Presidency Bank era.
questions.hint: Compare the four milestone years.

description: Exam-focused questions covering major institutions, milestones, reforms and chronology in Indian banking history.
